source: fccb30810 (2026-11-05) transfer of the P/08 N4 refusal tables into forms/refusals.tsv; judge P08.25 M1 (sentence rewritten: the cells are normative text, a repeated row number selects one condition)
removed: Original normative cells are preserved; repeated row numbers select the original condition and its operation-specific projection.
The rules of the module are [P/01.1 N0](../../01-store/spec/01.1-store.norms.md#n0-vocabulary).
The order of output arrays is P/08.0 N0 «Order of output arrays» (scope — lessons 8–10).
- `ENTRY_MAX` — a write after which the Entry is larger than `ENTRY_MAX` is not written: 409 «the entry of `<member>` would exceed ENTRY_MAX bytes».
- `ENTRY_MAX` — a row of 524288 bytes holds ≈ 420 Entry of the worst size; the average at 250,000 members — 61.
- `MEMBERS_MAX` — a limit of a section row, not of the domain: the ceiling of P/01.1 N1; the domain — ≈ 1.4 million at an average of 350 per row.
- `MEMBERS_MAX` — keep `SERVERS_MAX` equal to `MISSING_SHOWN` (P/08.5 N1.3 result): raised alone, it would take silent servers beyond the cut list, while the readers judge servers.

- `revoked_keys` — a report with a pushed-out key: on a write with key — 403 «the entry has no key or the key does not match» (chapter 8.3 N2); on a write without key — a knock, the admission refuses by revoked_members of the set (chapter 8.3 N3 step 4).
- `every_entry` — for Entry.ca after an accepted report (chapter 8.3 N1.6 on_accept), an Entry larger than ENTRY_MAX is not 409: the report is accepted, nothing changes, the log.
- `idem.IDEM_KEEP` — the row is removed by the holder pass (chapter 8.1 N3) with the turn guard, by the local monotonic age from the first observation of the row version.
- `idem.IDEM_KEEP` — a new process counts the age anew: the term is only longer.
- `idem.IDEM_MAX` — rows: an edit every 21 s around the clock.
- `idem.IDEM_MAX` — the count is the listing of the pass plus own writes after it.
- `idem.IDEM_MAX` — at the ceiling a key with a ready row answers from the memory, a door without a key works: the ceiling protects the store, not the edits.
- `turn` — own — CAS of the read version (N3 step 2), a foreign one unchanged ≥ TURN_TERM — take.
- `turn` — holder of the row — the process instance `<box>:<pid>:<6 hex>` (the instance form — the instance contract, common/contracts/instance.md).
- `guard` — the guard refused — the process stops being active.
- `objects` — rev-* of a backup copy is written by put_new: a deposed one does not overwrite the object of the new active one, the object exists — a conflict.
- `objects` — the new active one wrote the mutable object after our confirmation — our put_at gets conflict: do not write, re-read the turn.

- `objects` — the new active one wrote the mutable object before our confirmation — the confirmation itself does not pass (get_at after the confirmation\n  would leave a window — a pause between them would give the index of a write already made by the new active one, and put_at would overwrite it).

- `window` — the residual window: an object that the new active one has not touched yet, the put_at of the deposed process lets through — such a\n  write is the last one anyway, the next pass of the turn holder corrects it (the view — by recomputation, the mark — by the next\n  admission, the history — by appending).
- `standby` — a process without the turn is standby: it runs no pass.

- `standby` — `<instance>` in detail — its own, of the standby one that answered (the instance contract): the turn holder in detail\n  is not named — with an unreadable or given-up turn it is unknown.

- `no_signer` — the turn is for the whole process and without a condition on domain/signer: the process takes and confirms domain/signer-turn even without\n  the signer row (the target of a handover and of a move is a cluster without the holder keys, chapter 8.8).

- `no_signer` — without a readable domain/signer, POST /api/prepare, /api/take and /domain/move answer on\n  the merits in their own order (chapter 8.8 N1.7, N1.8: root, set, signature, record — checks of the doors themselves),\n  their writes — under the turn guard (guard).
- `no_signer` — without a readable domain/signer, the other doors of the process — 503 standby, as at a standby one.

- `fresh_turn` — the limit: a process stopped between the check and the answer can answer 200 after the loss\n  of the turn — the answer window of a door is not bounded; the keys are the same, the harm is «two answer».
